title: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused ops, rotary/rope support and KV-aware scheduling
author: Asha Rao
description:
Motivation: Upgrade the serving runtime attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 and enable a set of fused operations and rotary/rope improvements to reduce memory bandwidth, improve throughput for long-context workloads, and make KV cache interactions more efficient. This PR integrates kernel changes, runtime scheduling hooks, and continuous-batching adjustments so that the runtime can route KV-heavy requests to the new kernels while preserving correctness for legacy configs.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused qkv and rotary/rope-friendly code paths (CUDA/C++). 2) Add kernel selection logic in runtime to pick fused vs. compat kernels based on model metadata and request patterns. 3) KV-cache metadata changes: explicit per-request KV layout markers and lightweight validation to allow zero-copy KV accesses where supported. 4) Scheduler/policy updates: new KV-aware scheduling heuristic that groups requests by active KV-size and recent sequence-length distribution to improve batching efficiency. 5) Continuous-batching: improvements to batch formation timeout heuristics to prefer grouping rotary/rope-compatible workloads. 6) Tests and benchmarks: unit tests, integration tests against small/medium/long contexts, and end-to-end perf harness changes.

Benchmarks (canary results): A100 80GB, 8-token prompt, 2048 token generations - using new fused kernels with KV-aware scheduling we see: median throughput +1.8x, p50 latency down ~18%, p99 latency down ~12% for multi-turn conversational workloads with long KV caches. Memory footprint reduction on peak allocations ~10-15% in our canary.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `use_flashattnv2_fused` defaulted off. Rolling canary to 5% of traffic (dedicated fleet) for 72 hours, monitor token-level latency, model quality regressions, and end-to-end error rates. If green, increase to 25% then 100%. Emergency rollback via runtime flag and model routing policy.

Compatibility/Risks: New kernels require CUDA 11.8+ and cuBLAS/cuDNN versions in installers; installer notes added. For some older model variants we fall back to compat kernels automatically. There is a small risk of subtle numerical diffs for rotary implementations; added regression evals to detect quality drift.

Testing: added unit tests under tests/attention and integration tests in perf-canary harness. CI includes a gpu-smoke job and a perf-regression job.

Related: Linear tasks ENG-1425 (kernel upgrade), ENG-1602 (scheduling heuristics). Support ticket SUP-7881 reported elevated latency for long-context retrieval workloads which motivated parts of the scheduler changes.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel code and CMake changes - [x] Runtime kernel selection + config flag - [x] KV-cache metadata schema + validation - [x] Scheduler heuristics + continuous-batching adjustments - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks and canary plan - [x] Release notes and installer compatibility docs
commits: add flashattnv2 fused kernels and test harness (cuda/attn/kernels/*)
runtime: add kernel selector and feature flag for flashattnv2 fused path
kv-cache: add layout metadata + zero-copy validation hooks
scheduler: kv-aware grouping heuristic and continuous-batching timeout adjustments
tests: perf harness updates and regression evals
review_comments: Michael Chen: Left a few comments on the CUDA kernels around shared memory usage. Please double-check bank conflict patterns and add a short comment explaining the lane tiling choice.
Asha Rao: Replied: adjusted tiling to 128x4, added comments and a micro-benchmark in tests/attention to validate no regressions in bank conflicts.
Liam O'Neill: Scheduler changes look good overall. Can we add a metric for 'kv-grouped-batch-rate' to the runtime metrics to observe grouping effectiveness?
Asha Rao: Added metric 'runtime.attn.kv_grouped_batch_rate' and exposed it in the per-route dashboard. Updated rollout checklist to monitor it.

release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV and rotary/rope-friendly code paths. Expect ~1.8x throughput improvement and p99 latency improvements for long-context workloads on supported GPUs.
Ops: New runtime flag `use_flashattnv2_fused` to gate rollout. Installer compatibility: CUDA 11.8+ required for fused kernels.
